result.title: Progressive Permutation Alignment with Temperature-Controlled Spectral Sharpening
result.summary: In implicit neural representations (INRs), 3D signals are encoded directly in network weights, making stable weight-space operations essential. However, permutation symmetry causes independently trained yet functionally equivalent models to appear distant in weight space, often inducing large loss barriers under linear interpolation. Existing neuron alignment methods either commit early to discrete matches and become trapped in inconsistent local optima or rely on computationally expensive gradient optimization over continuous relaxations, both of which are unreliable in challenging cases such as NeRF. We adopt progressive alignment, a layer-wise strategy that follows inter-layer dependencies from input to output. At each layer, a correlation matrix is estimated and aligned with a discrete anchor obtained by the Hungarian algorithm, after which temperature-controlled spectral annealing gradually sharpens the correlation structure toward a permutation matrix. This update is deterministic and lightweight, avoiding the inner-loop gradient optimization required by continuous relaxation methods. A final refinement stage further optimizes the network layer-by-layer via weight matching, starting from the aligned solution. Experiments on MLPs, CNNs, and Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) show that the proposed method reliably recovers neuron correspondences and achieves stable alignment across architectures. In practical experiments aligning independently trained NeRF models, our method reduces the loss barriers under weight interpolation compared with existing approaches.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究隐式神经表示中的权重空间置换对称问题，提出按层递进的对齐方法：逐层估计相关矩阵并用 Hungarian 结果作离散锚点，再以温度控制的光谱退火逐步锐化为置换矩阵，最后做权重匹配精修，在 MLP、CNN 与 NeRF 上验证独立训练模型的对齐效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 置换对称导致功能等价的网络在权重空间看似远离，这一视角可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度比较（跨模型、跨层状态匹配）是否被排列不确定性混淆；其逐层对齐与退火锐化流程或可启发状态对应关系的求解，但与原论文的推理期 latent 生成无直接联系。
